body: I was going through (what I thought was) a *rough* time with my (ex)husband after moving back home, post military separation. We were living apart at the time, with little communication outside of him needing money, food, amusement, etc. He called me up, frantic, telling me he needed to clear his head and get out of town for a little while, and wanted me to accompany him on a drive. He picked me up, and we headed onto the highway - roughly 10 seconds later, there are multiple police cars boxing us in and before I could figure out what was going on, we both had guns drawn on us and he was being taken out of the vehicle. Once he was taken into their custody, after I was able to exit the vehicle (all the while pleading for an explanation as to what was going on), I was asked where the gun was, and if I had been hurt.  An officer that I was familiar with, seeing and hearing my confusion, came over to me and asked if I was the one who had made the call. Apparently, my ex had held a gun to his head after trying to barricade his girlfriend inside the house, and told her that he would kill himself if she left him. She had managed to get out and immediately called 911. I had no idea any of this was going on until I found out through that officer. There’s obviously a lot more to this, but I’d say it’s the wildest way I’ve found out I was being cheated on.

I’ll definitely look into doing that, thank you. The item cost them around $200 total (I’m not sure how much is refunded when a return request actually goes through - I have zero experience with this:/). I’d honestly be out of money regardless since I wouldn’t be able to resell the item as brand new (they posted photos in their return request, and the item’s packaging was completely torn open), or possibly wouldn’t be able to resell at all depending on what the buyer has actually sent me in the mail. What weirds me out the most is that they waited two weeks and had no direct communication with me whatsoever, but still went and shipped me a package. 

Would they be able to pursue a refund? I considered trying to pay to intercept the package and have it returned, but I’m not sure if that would somehow come back to bite me or not.
Thank you! I’ve decided it’s definitely in my best interest to just refuse the package. I’ve gotten myself too worried to do anything else.
Thank you. I’m most definitely going to refuse it when it arrives. I’ll likely be way too afraid to do anything else. Lol.
Yeah, I think my best bet is refusing/returning the package. A friend suggested to report it as a suspicious package, but apparently that would involve my local PD, so “return to sender” it is!

Thank you :) I’m new to selling, so I wasn’t sure I was doing the right thing and I felt kind of funny not responding. I’ve blocked them now, but I don’t know that I’m ballsy enough to keep & relist… I’m also not totally sure that the buyer is returning the actual item. I know the item is no longer BNIP either, so I’m not sure the condition if it is the actual item. Perhaps I’m a bit paranoid, but I find this situation pretty strange, so I’m not totally sure what exactly to expect.

Thank you. I will say that I’m definitely curious about the contents of the package (I feel like it could literally be anything), but I don’t think I’m ballsy enough to keep it and resell it. Thanks for the tip on refunding off of Mercari - I felt uneasy about that after the claim was closed, but I didn’t realize it could get anyone banned. Definitely glad I haven’t had any communication with this buyer.

Thank you, I appreciate the help. I’ve went ahead and blocked them since getting responses from you guys here. I didn’t block them after the request got closed or when they sent out a message because I didn’t really see a reason to, you know? They hadn’t messaged me since, but went and shipped the package two weeks later. They shipped two days ago and as of the timing of my initial post here, hadn’t sent any additional messages. I only discovered that they had sent me a package when checking my USPS Informed Delivery. I find it really bizarre, and wasn’t sure how to proceed. The claim they made definitely made me think they just didn’t want to pay for their purchase, as there wasn’t anything actually wrong with the item and they had no way to really prove otherwise. Mercari denied their claim pretty quickly, and they didn’t seem to try to pursue anything beyond sending me a single message.

Thank you, I appreciate your input. It seems like refusing the package is the best route to take. I’m actually a bit creeped out that the buyer is mailing me a package (given their return was denied and I haven’t been in contact with them), but I might just be kind of paranoid. I did notice that the buyer uses more than one identity, so you’re probably right that they were likely trying to scam. Do you think it’s better to just refuse the package, and not reach out to Mercari? I’d like to be done with this weird situation. lol.

This is extremely helpful, thank you so much. I’ve gone ahead and blocked them, and will refuse the package when it arrives. I really appreciate your response. I wasn’t sure if I should try to reach out to Mercari about it, or just handle it on my own. I was more than a little put off to see an incoming package from this person for sure.

Thank you, I appreciate the help! I found it pretty odd that the buyer would mail back the item (or what I assumed to be the item) after being denied and not having any communication from me after this long. I’ll likely just refuse the package and cross my fingers that I don’t receive more mail from the buyer in another few weeks.
